# CSSX-TT5 — Cross-runtime and consumer matrix

**Phase:** TT5 of `.ai/plans/CSSX-PLAN-TESTING.md` · **Status:** 🟡 complete for the owned scope, with
three rows recorded **UNVERIFIED** and one documentation finding for TT8 (TT5 row left 🔴 for build to
flip after independent verification)
**Date:** 2026-11-25 · **Tree:** `main`, uncommitted · **Scope:** new files under
`tests/stress/consumer/**` only + this report

## Summary

- Every plan §TT5 row is implemented as an executed, seeded case: **9 new files, 38 tests, 1 149
  assertions, 4.0 s**. Two of them (`decode.ts`, `normalize.ts`) are hand-written oracles so no
  dependency was added and no oracle shares code with the artifact it judges.
- Runtime matrix actually available here: **Node 23.1.0, 24.22.3, 26.13.1 and Bun 1.4.5** — all four
  import the **built** `@xessa/compiler` from `dist/` and run `dist/index.js --version`. **Node 20 and
  Node 22 are not installed on this machine and are recorded UNVERIFIED with that reason**, never as
  passed (the plan's exit criterion for this phase).
- Generated artifacts hold up outside Bun: literal `.d.ts` inference, `@ts-expect-error` behaviour,
  1000-file emitted CSS re-parsed by the built parser **and** by `xessa check`, byte-for-byte minify
  parity (234 025 B pretty → 182 025 B minified, 0 structural differences), and declaration-level
  source maps decoded by an independent VLQ decoder at 1/100/1000 files (**11 000 segments, 0 out of
  bounds, hand-picked declarations on their authored positions**).
- **One finding for TT8** (documentation, not a compiler defect): a generated map with the default
  `import-css: true` emits `import "…/file.css";`, which plain Node executes as
  `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION`. Node consumers need a bundler or a CSS-loader hook; `import-css: false`
  produces a dependency-free map Node imports directly. Neither `docs/compatibility.md` nor
  `docs/known-limitations.md` states this today. No compiler source is changed here.
- Gates: `bun test tests/stress/consumer/` **38 pass / 0 fail**; `bun run lint` **exit 0**;
  `bun run verify` **1 160 pass / 0 fail (83 files, 35.65 s)** — the TT0 baseline was 1 122 pass over
  77 files, and no sibling suite regressed.

Rows above are generated by `runtimeMatrix()` in `tests/stress/consumer/helpers.ts`; the Node 20/22
rows exist precisely so their absence is asserted, not skipped. Discovery scans `PATH`, the
nvm/fnm/asdf/volta/mise layouts and the directory of the running test binary, canonicalizes, dedupes
and requires a parseable `--version`. `~/.nvm/versions/node/v23.6.0` exists but has no `bin/node`, so
it is filtered out by the existence/`--version` probe rather than reported. A second Bun shim
(`…/v23.1.0/lib/node_modules/bun/bin/bun.exe`, 1.1.45) is discovered; the matrix selects the binary
that is running the suite (`process.execPath` → 1.4.5). No runtime below the `engines.node` floor was
found, so the exclusion list is empty.

## Minify-parity method

- Both artifacts come from the **same** generated project (`thousandFileProject`, seed
  `XESSA_STRESS_SEED=1`, label `consumer/minify-parity`) compiled twice through the built `dist`
  (`output.minify: false` / `true`), so the only input difference is the flag.
- Both outputs are re-parsed with the built `parse()` and reduced by `tests/stress/consumer/normalize.ts`
  to `{kind, selector|name+prelude, declarations[], children[]}` with whitespace runs collapsed to one
  space and trimmed. That is the *only* tolerated difference, because
  `docs/configuration.md:43` documents minify as "compact generated structural whitespace; authored
  tokens and declaration order are preserved" and `docs/cascade.md:22` makes authored declaration order
  part of the contract — so **no sorting, no dedup, order-sensitive comparison**.
- Numbers (this machine, default seed): **pretty 234 025 B → minified 182 025 B** (−52 000 B, −22.2 %);
  1000/1000 entries structurally identical; 0 parser errors on either side; per-file structure is
  5 rules / 6 declarations / 1 `@media` (aggregate 5 000 / 6 000 / 1 000, asserted exactly).
- Anti-vacuity: hand-built pairs prove the normalizer tolerates `.a{display:flex;padding:4px;}` vs the
  indented form but detects a swapped declaration order, a changed value and a changed selector. The
  exact byte totals are asserted as bounds (`< prettier`, saving > 20 000 B, > pretty/2) rather than
  frozen numbers, because the generator is seeded and its padding values may change with the seed.

## VLQ decoder notes

`tests/stress/consumer/decode.ts` is a from-scratch decoder (base64 alphabet, continuation bit 32,
sign bit in the LSB, 5-bit groups) that never imports `@xessa/compiler`, so an encoder bug cannot hide
behind a shared assumption. It also rejects malformed input instead of guessing: an unknown base64
character, a truncated trailing group, or a segment that is not exactly four fields throws.
`decodeMappings` accumulates generated column per line (reset each line) and source index / source
line / source column across the document, per the v3 specification. Positions are zero-based, matching
the payload; `zeroBasedPosition()` converts an authored or emitted UTF-16 offset into that convention
with its own line walker (no compiler helper reused).

Sanity of the decode is itself asserted: `sourcesContent[0]` must equal the authored source text, and
every segment must land inside the emitted artifact it claims to describe (line/column bounds) — which
is how a subtly wrong delta accumulation would surface as "column beyond end of line".

Pinned mapping granularity (documented in `packages/compiler/src/sourcemaps/mappings.ts`, verified at
scale here): one mapping per emitted **rule selector** and one per emitted **declaration property**. A
rule selector maps to its declaration run's origin (i.e. its first declaration), and an inline variant
maps to its modifier (`@md`) origin — so `.card-0001 {` on line 0 maps to the authored `display`
position, not to the authored selector. Both behaviours are asserted, not just recorded.

## Findings for TT8

**F1 — generated maps with `import-css: true` are not plain-Node importable (documentation gap).**
Repro (recorded live in `esm-consumer.test.ts:187`):

```console
$ node --input-type=module -e 'await import("file:///…/dist/maps/src/card.map.js")'
TypeError [ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION]: Unknown file extension ".css" for …/dist/styles/src/card.css
# exit 1
$ XESSA_MAP_MODULE=… node node-import-css.mjs        # module.registerHooks / register CSS stub
{"default":{"card-one":"ui-card-one",…},"named":{…}}  # exit 0
```

Bun imports the same map with no loader. Expected for a bundler target, but neither
`docs/compatibility.md:71-74` ("Compiler runtime ✅ Node ≥ 20 and Bun"; "Node package entry ✅
Node-compatible") nor `docs/known-limitations.md` states that the map's stylesheet import needs a
bundler/CSS-loader under Node, or that `import-css: false` yields a Node-importable map. Suggested
TT8 action: add a `docs/known-limitations.md` row (and cross-link from `docs/compatibility.md`
"Class map" row), or decide to keep the CSS import out of the map. No compiler source touched here.

**F2 — "Node ≥ 20" remains partially unverified.** `docs/compatibility.md:71` and the root
`engines.node` claim Node ≥ 20, but only Node 23/24/26 and Bun exist on this machine. TT5 extends the
recorded evidence to 23.1.0 / 24.22.3 / 26.13.1; **20 and 22 must stay listed as unverified** until a
machine with those majors runs `bun test tests/stress/consumer/`. TT8 should refresh
`docs/compatibility.md` with the actual matrix rather than the single 24.22.3 datapoint.

**F3 — no independent CSS parser (accepted limitation).** The plan's CSS-validity half that asks for a
third-party parser stays unimplemented by design; the oracle is the compiler's own parser plus the CLI
`xessa check` path (same parser family), so a parser bug that also accepts invalid CSS would not be
caught. Same limitation as the TT2 report (`CSSX-TT2.md`, "Emitted-CSS validation" note).

**F4 — bundler row unexercised.** `esbuild`/`vite` are absent and may not be installed, so the
bundling half of the ESM-consumer row is recorded unverified. `esm-consumer.test.ts:282` pins the
absence (tool status and `package.json` must agree), so the row cannot silently turn into a pass; a
future environment with a bundler needs the bundling branch implemented (a task, not this phase).

**Method note — `xessa check` cannot check `.css` directly.** `xessa check` type-checks authored
`.cssx` sources, so case 16 re-authors every emitted stylesheet as a `.cssx` source (emitted CSS parses
as CSSX; strategy `none`, no `dist`) and asserts the CLI reports 0 errors/0 warnings over all 1000. The
limitation is that this validates *parse/compile* acceptance of the emitted text, not a CSS-grammar
conformance claim beyond what the compiler accepts.

**Pinned behavior worth keeping in mind for TT8 (not to "fix").** `@media` preludes are not mapped
(only selectors/declarations are), and rule selectors map to their first declaration span — both
documented in `packages/compiler/src/sourcemaps/mappings.ts` and asserted here at scale.

## Deviations and recorded limitations

1. **`bun run release:check` not run.** It re-runs the browser matrix and rebuilds `examples/*/generated`
   (committed artifacts) plus `packages/vscode` — write targets outside TT5's scope
   (`tests/stress/consumer/**` + this report). Packaging metadata is unchanged by this phase, so the
   packaging gate is deferred to the production plan's PP0, which the testing plan already requires
   after TT7.
2. **Node 20 and Node 22 unverified.** No binary on this machine; recorded as unverified with the
   reason in both the matrix and case 3. Nothing in the suite claims they pass.
3. **Extra runtimes added instead of inventing rows.** Node 23.1.0 and 26.13.1 are reported as extra,
   non-required rows and are fully exercised — that is the "full matrix that IS available" the task
   asked for.
4. **Bundler and third-party-parser rows recorded unverified** (F3/F4); no tool was installed.
5. **`dist/` is rebuilt by the suite** through the standard build command when stale. `dist/` is
   gitignored (`git check-ignore` confirms), so no tracked file is touched.
6. **Byte totals are bounds, not frozen constants**, because the generator is seeded (a different
   `XESSA_STRESS_SEED` changes padding values). Structure counts are asserted exactly (5 000 rules /
   6 000 declarations / 1 000 at-rules).
